decisions.executionNote: Begin raising and tilting the right gripper toward the basket with small continuous elbow-up motions.
Advance above the back basket egg while rotating toward a downward grasp; keep left arm parked.
Align the downward right gripper over the rear egg, approaching slowly with the jaws open.
Refine the rear egg alignment from wrist RGB, shifting right before lowering the open jaws.
Close around the aligned rear egg and make a short retention-check lift; basket clearance is tight.
The egg was not retained. Reopen, follow its shifted position toward the basket center, and lower for a deeper grasp.
Refine the open-jaw alignment on the rear egg and descend 15 mm before closing.
Close around the now-centered egg and lift vertically to check retention before transport.
Egg appears retained. Lift clear and move inward, gradually angling the gripper for placement while keeping the right EE on its side.
Transport the retained egg toward the holder, rotating gradually to reach the central cups without moving the right arm across the left.
Lower the held egg toward the rear-right cup, keeping the right link6 to the right of center and checking cup alignment before release.
The egg has slipped to the right of the holder. Open and retreat upward to locate it for recovery.
Approach the loose egg on the table with open jaws, preserving the current angled grasp orientation.
Fine-align the loose egg between the fingertips and approach along the gripper axis before closing.
Advance the fingertips deeper around the egg, then close fully while keeping the wrist stationary.
Lift the recovered egg without changing orientation and check that it stays between the closed fingers.
The recovered egg remains visible between the fingers. Translate slowly over the rear-right holder cup without rotating the grasp.
The shallow grasp slipped during closure. Recover the loose egg with a deeper, vertical grasp rather than carrying it at the fingertips.
Track the loose egg as it settles and finish orienting the open right gripper vertically above it.
Lower the open vertical jaws well around the loose egg's equator, avoiding another shallow fingertip grasp.
At table clearance, center the egg inside the open paddles and close progressively without lifting yet.
The egg remains beyond the closed fingertips. Reopen and move the wrist toward the front so the egg lies deeper between the paddles.
The egg is now centered between the paddles in wrist RGB. Lower slightly, close fully, and begin a minimal retention-check lift.
Lift vertically with the gripper closed and unchanged orientation to verify a stable deeper grasp.
Carry the visibly retained egg toward the holder with gradual tilt and clearance; maintain a fully closed target.
The egg slipped on tilting. Return to a vertical gripper and approach the empty holder edge to improve right-side access before retrying.
Approach the empty holder's right wall with vertical open jaws, preparing to shift it into the right workspace.
Gently pinch the holder's right rim and test a small rightward slide; stop to inspect whether the holder follows.
Test a gentle rightward pull with the holder rim pinched, slightly lifting to clear the table.
Correct the rejected tensor; release the holder and return above the loose egg without changing orientation.
Center over the settled loose egg and lower open vertical paddles to grasp depth.
Shift the egg deeper between the paddles, close fully, and test a short vertical lift.
Lift the grasped egg clear and begin translating toward the holder with no wrist rotation to avoid the previous slip.
Continue a level, no-rotation transfer toward the nearest holder cup; egg remains visibly retained.
Approach the near-right cup with only a very slight, slow inward lean; keep link6 on the right side.
Lower toward the front-right cup while slowly leaning the retained egg inward to align its center with the opening.
The egg is aligned and appears supported in the front-right cup. Open the jaws fully, then lift away gently.
Withdraw from the released egg and return toward the basket, checking whether the egg settles correctly in the holder.
The released egg landed in front of the holder. Recover it and correct the next placement farther back and lower before opening.
Center the loose egg and lower the open paddles to the previously effective table grasp depth.
Move the egg deeper inside the open paddles and close fully at a fixed wrist pose.
Lift the recovered egg clear of the holder front wall before moving farther back over a cup.
Move farther over the holder at clearance height, slowly leaning inward while keeping the retained egg closed.
The egg now aligns over the front-right cup in the head view. Lower vertically toward the cup bottom without changing the grasp.
Contact has shifted the egg above the fingers. Open immediately over the cup and withdraw vertically to let it settle.
The released egg appears seated in the rear-right cup. Withdraw upward and move toward the basket with the same grasp orientation.
Approach the leftmost remaining basket egg with open jaws and the same slightly inward-leaning grasp orientation.
Replan from the interrupted pose: move more slowly above the basket rim, slightly lifting before descending onto the next egg.
Lower inside the basket toward the leftmost egg, correcting the open gripper slightly forward and right.
The left basket egg is centered between the open paddles. Lower around its equator, then close without moving the wrist.
Lift the second egg straight clear of the basket, keeping the closed grasp and wrist orientation unchanged.
The egg slipped during lifting. Reopen and approach the front basket egg more deeply, keeping the paddles clear of the rim.
Straighten the open gripper over the front egg and correct leftward alignment with small motions to avoid the basket rim.
The wide paddles appear blocked by the rim. Narrow the opening slightly and approach farther inside the basket before closing.
The front egg is centered between the narrowed paddles. Deepen slightly, then close fully without lifting.
Lift the centered egg slowly and vertically, holding the closed gripper and orientation fixed.
Move the visibly retained egg clear of the basket toward the holder with no change in grasp orientation.
The front egg slipped against the rim. Reopen and reposition above the basket's right egg with greater overhead clearance.
Align above the rightmost egg and descend with the paddles partly narrowed to clear the woven rim.
Lower deeper around the right egg, bringing it toward the center of the open paddles before closing.
The outer paddle is contacting the rim. Narrow the jaw gap and move toward the egg's center before a shallow final descent.
The egg shifted away from the shallow fingertips. Lift clear and make the gripper vertical for a direct descent around its center.
Descend vertically on the right egg while correcting its wrist-image alignment, keeping the paddles inside the rim.
Bring the right egg deeper between the paddles, lower around its sides, and close without lifting.
The egg is still beyond the fingertips. Reopen and move toward it from above before trying to close again.
Clear the obstructing front rim and reposition over the rear egg, which has more room for a deep grasp.
Move over the rear egg and descend vertically, keeping the opening wide enough to surround it.
Center the rear egg farther inside the paddles and lower slowly around its sides.
Back the paddles slightly around the rear egg's equator, then close fully at fixed height.
Lift the rear egg straight upward, keeping the closed grasp fixed until it clears the basket rim.
Raise the retained egg farther above the rim while beginning a slow inward transfer without rotating the wrist.
